rationale: C16 is a closely matched predecessor letter concerning designation to the identical office of Supreme Allied Commander, Europe. It supplies a concrete functional template: announce the personnel action, situate it within NATO, express confidence in allied support and the appointee's leadership, and close with personal approval or good wishes. Although the child is a shorter letter making Gruenther available for appointment rather than formally designating him, the shared office, institutional setting, and sequence make adaptation of C16 plausible. C04 is also structurally relevant but concerns a different NATO command and is dominated by formal command authorities absent from the child. C03 shares commendatory language but only generically.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am making you available for appointment as SACEUR to succeed General Ridgway.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: at their request I have designated you as Supreme Allied Commander, Europe.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters announce a presidential personnel action placing the addressee into the same NATO supreme command.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I anticipate unanimous desire for this action because of the outstanding importance you bring in continuing the effectiveness and solidarity of N.A.T.O.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I view their request as a pledge that their support of your efforts will be complete and unequivocal.
shared_material.explanation: Each connects the appointment with NATO-wide approval and support for the commander's efforts.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As Supreme Allied Commander, Europe, I know the fine traditions and worthy objectives sought by all the nations will be upheld and carried forward through your leadership.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You are undertaking a tremendous responsibility... our entire country is wholeheartedly behind you... I send you my warmest personal good wishes for success in the great task which awaits you.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by emphasizing the office's importance, confidence in the appointee, and personal presidential support.
